name: Texas
headline_status: Recreational marijuana is illegal; a limited low-THC medical program (TCUP) was expanded in 2025.
summary: Texas allows only low-THC medical cannabis through the Compassionate Use Program (TCUP). HB 46, which took effect September 1, 2025, added chronic pain and other conditions, allowed non-smoked inhaled products, and raised the number of licensed dispensing organizations from 3 to 15. Recreational possession is still a crime: two ounces or less is a Class B misdemeanor. Under state rules, hemp-derived THC can be sold only to adults 21 and over; since March 31, 2026 THCA counts toward the 0.3% delta-9 THC limit, which rules out most THCA flower, and since July 31, 2026 delta-8 and other non-delta-9 THCs are Schedule I.

medical_program.value: TCUP covers a defined list of conditions for permanent Texas residents. HB 46 (2025) added chronic pain lasting more than 90 days, traumatic brain injury, Crohn's disease or other inflammatory bowel disease, and terminal illness or hospice or palliative care. Smoking is excluded from medical use; a physician may prescribe inhaling an aerosol or vapor when it is medically necessary.

possession_limit.value: For TCUP products, HB 46 replaced the old 1% THC-by-weight cap with a limit of 10 mg THC per dose and no more than 1 gram of THC per package.

retail_sales.value: No adult-use sales. Medical sales come only from DPS-licensed dispensing organizations; HB 46 set a total of 15 licenses and allows satellite locations.

regulator.value: The Texas Department of Public Safety licenses TCUP dispensing organizations. The Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission and the Department of State Health Services regulate hemp-derived THC sales.

penalties.value: Possessing 2 ounces or less of marijuana is a Class B misdemeanor; more than 2 and up to 4 ounces is a Class A misdemeanor; larger amounts are felonies.

hemp_thc.value: Under Gov. Abbott's Executive Order GA-56 (Sept. 10, 2025), TABC and DSHS rules bar hemp product sales to anyone under 21 and require ID checks. DSHS rules in effect since March 31, 2026 count THCA toward the 0.3% delta-9 THC limit, which rules out most THCA flower and other smokable hemp; the rules are the subject of ongoing litigation. Since July 31, 2026, delta-8 and other THCs that are not delta-9 are treated as Schedule I controlled substances in Texas. Edibles and drinks may still be sold if they meet the 0.3% delta-9 THC limit.

purchase_age.value: 21 or older for hemp-derived THC products, with ID required for every sale at TABC-licensed retailers.

public_use.value: There is no legal recreational use. Compassionate Use Program patients may use only prescribed low-THC cannabis; smoking is excluded from medical use.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Texas has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DWI requires evidence of impairment.

tourists.value: No. There are no adult-use marijuana sales, and only permanent Texas residents can be prescribed low-THC cannabis through the Compassionate Use Program, so visitors face the same possession penalties as residents.

home_grow.value: Not allowed. Growing marijuana is prosecuted as possession, with penalties scaled by weight.

timeline.event: Gov. Abbott signs HB 46, expanding the Compassionate Use Program.
Gov. Abbott vetoes SB 3, which would have banned THC outside TCUP. Two special sessions end without a hemp bill.
Executive Order GA-56 directs TABC and DSHS to set a 21+ age limit and testing and packaging rules for hemp.
TABC adopts permanent hemp rules for its licensees.
DSHS rules counting THCA toward the 0.3% delta-9 THC limit take effect, ruling out most THCA flower and smokable hemp.

pending.item: Federal hemp redefinition: most of the new federal definition, which would remove most intoxicating consumable hemp THC products from legal hemp, takes effect on 11 December 2026; only the exclusion for cannabinoids the plant cannot produce naturally starts on 12 November 2026.
pending.status: Delayed from 12 November by Pub. L. 119-103 (signed 2 September 2026), per the Congressional Research Service.

faq.a: No. Recreational marijuana is illegal, and possessing up to 2 ounces is a Class B misdemeanor. Only low-THC medical cannabis through TCUP is legal.

Yes, in limited form, for permanent Texas residents. The Compassionate Use Program allows low-THC cannabis for listed conditions; since 2025 these include chronic pain lasting more than 90 days, traumatic brain injury, Crohn's disease or other inflammatory bowel disease, and terminal illness or hospice or palliative care. Smoking is excluded, though a physician may prescribe an inhaled aerosol or vapor when medically necessary.

faq.q: Is THCA flower legal in Texas?
faq.a: Mostly not. Since March 31, 2026, state health rules count THCA toward the 0.3% delta-9 THC limit, which rules out most THCA flower; the rules are the subject of ongoing litigation.

faq.q: How old do you have to be to buy delta-8 or hemp THC in Texas?
faq.a: 21, under rules adopted after the governor's September 2025 executive order, and stores must check ID.
